_note: Tracked-thread id sets (ARCHITECTURE.md plan B, 2026-09-27). Derived from pipeline/thread-stems.json's stem policy via bible-core's tools/stems_to_roots.py -- every id here is a lemma id in Matthew-words.tsv, checked against exactly one other root's claim (biblecore.roots.validate). Six of thread-stems.json's seven 'phrase: true' threads really are fixed multi-word titles and use `seq` instead of `ids` (plan D2): son-of-man, son-of-david, law-prophets, apo-tote, completion-of-age, weeping-grinding. The seventh, little-faith (oligopistoi), turned out on inspection to be one compound Greek word, not a phrase -- an ordinary `ids` entry below.

acts-of-power.note: dynamis — 'act of power, mighty work.' Kept literal rather than 'miracle' (which implies a modern category of the supernatural Matthew doesn't use) or 'power' alone (which loses the countable, event-shaped sense — these are things done, plural).

anxious.note: Promoted from unit-06's local palette when merimnaō recurred at 10:19. Related to merizō, 'to divide' — kept as the clumsier 'pulled apart with care' rather than smoother 'worry' or 'anxious,' to keep the division-sense visible.

apo-tote.note: Two 'from that time' hinges: 4:17 ('began to proclaim') <-> 16:21 ('began to show he must suffer'). Read the two together at Unit 17. gap set to 1 (adjacent only) -- 'apo' and 'tote' are both far too common separately to risk the default gap of 4. Book-wide this is exactly 3 occurrences: 4:17, 16:21, and 26:16 (Judas) -- the third isn't in threads.json's payoffs list but is the same idiom.

authority.note: The crowds marvel that he teaches with authority (7:29); it runs to the mountain of commission (28:18).

build.note: The wise builder builds on rock (7:24) -> 'I will build my assembly' (16:18).

call.note: kaleō — the naming at 1:21 ('you shall call his name Jesus') becomes the calling of the unworthy (9:13) and the vocabulary of the kingdom's invitations. Distinct from prefixed compounds (parakaleō 'urge', proskaleomai 'summon', ekklēsia 'assembly'), each its own word.

clean.note: Promoted from unit-08's local palette when katharizō recurred in the mission charge at 10:8.

come-here.note: deute — 'come here, and I will make you fishers of men' (4:19) is the thread's true open; the invitation returns at 11:28 to all who labor.

completion-of-age.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): fixed phrase synteleia tou aiōnos. Opens in a harvest parable, closes as the horizon of the Emmanuel promise. Ahead: 24:3; 28:20.

counsel.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). The leaders 'take counsel' — 12:14, 22:15, 27:1, 27:7, 28:12: the plot from the Sabbath healing to the bribed guards.

cross.note: stauros — first at 10:38 as a general condition of following, well before any passion prediction; recurs at 16:24 and then the crucifixion itself.

defame.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). Rendered 'defame' (not the loan-word 'blaspheme'; not 'slander', which is kept for diabolos). 9:3 changed from 'blasphemes' to match. Ahead: 15:19, 26:65, 27:39.

enemy.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): echthros / echthra. Ahead: 22:44.

evil.note: ponēros — tagged from its first occurrence (5:11) but the tracked thread proper opens at the Lord's Prayer's 'deliver us from the evil one' (6:13), which the Sermon and the parables keep answering.

eye.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): a unit-07 local root recurring at 13:15–16. ophthalmos, every form.

faith.note: The centurion's pistis (8:10, 'not even in Israel') vs. the disciples' oligopistoi (see little-faith). Runs through the healings to 15:28 and the mountain-moving sayings.

father.note: patēr — tagged at every occurrence including the ordinary human sense (2:22, Herod's father); the tracked thread proper opens at 5:16, 'your Father who is in the skies,' Matthew's characteristic address for God.

fear.note: phobeō — the mē phobeisthe imperative saturates 10:26-31 and then recurs verbatim at the two most loaded moments, the sea (14:27) and the empty tomb (28:5, 10).

fish.note: 'Fishers of men' (4:19) carries OT judgement freight (Jer 16:16; Hab 1; Amos 4; Ezek 29) in tension with gathering-for-restoration.

follow.note: Used of the four (4:20, 22) AND of the crowds (4:25); the ambiguity is what 5:1 opens on. A discipleship keyword from Unit 4 on.

foolish.note: The foolish builder on sand (7:26); 'fools and blind' (23:17); the five foolish virgins (25:2).

fringe.note: kraspedon — the tzitzit of Numbers 15:38. Touched in faith and healing at 9:20 and 14:36; worn for display at 23:5.

fruit.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20): unit-07 local root recurring at 12:33.

fulfill.note: plēroō — the formula-quotation verb (1:22 and on) becomes Jesus' own stated relationship to the Law and the Prophets (5:17).

gather.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): synagō · episynagō; synagōgē (synagogue) is a separate word and not tagged. John's harvest (3:12) is reframed as delayed at 13:30. Ahead: 22:10–34; 24:28, 31; 25:24–26.

gehenna.note: geenna — the Hinnom Valley's name for judgment, first at 5:22 (the Sermon's escalating anger-warnings), returning at 10:28 and the woes of 23.

generation.note: genea shifts from the literal genealogical generations of 1:17 to a moral class of people, opening its tracked sense at 11:16 ('this generation'). The 1:17 occurrence is tagged for lexical completeness, not claimed as the same sense.

gentle.note: praeis — 'blessed are the gentle' (5:5) is the thread's true open; Jesus claims the word of himself at 11:29.

good-news.note: euangelion — the summary refrain of 4:23/9:35 becomes John's own answer at 11:5, then a global horizon (24:14) and the woman's memorial (26:13).

hand-over.note: paradidōmi — Judas is introduced by it at 10:4, then it fires three times for the disciples (10:17, 19, 21); from 17:22 on it becomes the governing verb of the passion.

harvest.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): a unit-10 local root that recurred at 13:30, 39. therismos · theristēs · therizō. Ahead: reaping where you did not sow (25:24, 26).

heart.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): kardia, every form. Ahead: 15:8–19 (heart vs lips; what defiles) and 22:37 (the Shema).

hide.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): kryptō and compounds; a unit-11 local root that recurred at 13:33, 35, 44. Ahead: the talent hidden in the ground (25:18, 25).

house.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). oikia · oikos and oikiakos ('household'); oikodespotēs ('master of the house') is not tagged. Ahead: 'y'all's house is left desolate' (23:38).

householder.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): oikodespotēs. The learner becomes like his master (10:25 → 13:52). The `house` thread deliberately excludes it. Ahead: 20:1, 11; 21:33; 24:43.

immerse.note: Promoted from unit-03's local palette when the noun baptistēs ('Immerser') recurred as John's title at 11:11-12. Rendered 'immerse / Immerser' throughout — never 'baptize / Baptist' — to keep the ordinary washing-verb sense audible.

joy.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): chara and chairō ('rejoice'; also the 'Hail!' greetings at 26:49, 27:29). Rootless joy (13:20) against joy that sells everything (13:44). Ahead: 25:21, 23 and 28:8.

judge.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20): a unit-07 local root that recurred through 10:15, 11:22–24 and all of 12. krinō · krisis · kritēs · katakrinō; 5:40 krithēnai is rendered 'sue' (go to law).

kingdom.note: basileia — 'the kingdom of the skies has drawn near' (3:2, 4:17) governs the Sermon's beatitudes and the parables to come. Distinct from basileus 'king' (10:18, 17:25, 18:23, 22:2), a different word not tracked here.

law-prophets.note: Frames the body of the Sermon, opened 5:17 and closed 7:12. Spanned Units 5-7; now closed. Matched in this order (5:17, 7:12, 22:40); 11:13 reverses the pair ('all the prophets and the law') and is NOT caught by this seq -- a single ordered seq can't cover both orders. Tagged by hand there; a known audit gap, not a missing occurrence.

lawlessness.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): anomia. Four occurrences, all at moments of judgment. Ahead: 23:28; 24:12.

learn.note: mathētēs — 'learner,' from manthanō, 'to learn.' Rendered 'learner' rather than the loan-word 'disciple' throughout the running translation, to keep the ordinary sense of the word audible.

light.note: Isa 9 light dawns on the people (4:16) -> 'y'all are the light of the world' (5:14). Watch the light/dark pair across the 4/5 seam.

little-faith.note: Matthew's near-nickname for the disciples (oligopistoi). Distinct from the `faith` thread (pistis, the centurion's) — different word, own colour.

lose.note: apollymi — the lost sheep (10:6), then the losing that is done on purpose (10:39) and a reward never lost (10:42); the lost sheep returns at 15:24 and 18:12-14.

mercy.note: Hosea 6:6 (eleos = LXX for hesed, covenant loyalty, not mere pity): 'I want loyal-love and not sacrifice.' Cited at 9:13, repeated at 12:7, cried out at 9:27.

metanoia.note: metanoeite — John's proclamation (3:2), repeated on Jesus' own lips (4:17), returns as an indictment on the unrepentant towns (11:20).

nations.note: 'Galilee of the nations' (4:15) -> 'make disciples of all the nations' (28:19). One leg of the Emmanuel/nations frame around the whole book.

peace.note: 'Blessed are the peacemakers' (5:9) sets up the mission discourse's harder word: the peace a household may not deserve, and the sword Jesus says he brings instead (10:34).

permitted.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). The legal-question verb; every Matthean use is a dispute over what Torah allows (14:4, 19:3, 20:15, 22:17, 27:6).

raise.note: egeirō spans the mundane (get up, rouse from sleep, 1:24) and the resurrection sense it grows into. Every occurrence tagged; the trajectory is 1:24 -> the healings -> 16:21 -> the empty tomb.

release.note: Same verb for letting go a debt, a fever, a boat, the dead. Unit 6 prayer -> Unit 8 healings -> Unit 9 forgiveness.

rest.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). Ahead: 'sleep on and take rest' (26:45).

righteous.note: dikaios / dikaiosynē — Joseph 'a righteous man' (1:19) opens it; the Sermon makes righteousness the thing hungered for, persecuted for, and exceeded (5:6-20), then sought first (6:33).

rock.note: The house founded on petra (7:24-25) -> Peter the rock (16:18). Distinct from Petros, the name.

rotten.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): sapros. Rotten tree and worthless catch share one verdict word.

save.note: sōzō — 'he will save his people from their sins' (1:21) carries a heal/rescue double sense Matthew never forces apart, running to the irony at the cross.

sea.note: Sea/Galilee geography in Unit 4; in Unit 8 the sea becomes a chaos-and-authority stage.

seek.note: zēteō — Herod seeks the child to destroy him (2:13); the Sermon turns the same verb toward the kingdom (6:33) and toward prayer itself (7:7).

shake.note: The 'great seismos' on the sea (8:24) is the same word as the earthquakes at the cross and the tomb.

sign.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). The sign of Jonah; returns at 16:1–4, 24:3, 24:24, 24:30 and Judas's sign (26:48).

sin.note: hamartia / hamartōlos — named at 1:21 as the thing the whole rescue is aimed at ('he will save his people from their sins'), not political liberation. Runs through John's baptism of confession (3:6) to Unit 9, where releasing sins and healing a body are made one act (9:2-6) and the sinners themselves are who Jesus says he came to call (9:10-13), and lands at the cup (26:28). Pairs with save (1:21) and release (aphiēmi, 9:2).

skandalon.note: skandalizō — the eye/hand that trips you up (5:29-30) is the thread's true open; the little beatitude of 11:6 warns John gently, then 26:31-33 pays it off catastrophically.

snatch.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): harpazō and compounds (diarpazō); harpax ('ravenous', 7:15) deliberately left untagged. A tight three-unit arc: the kingdom snatched, the strong man plundered, the seed snatched back.

son-of-david.note: First direct address at 9:27, always a cry from the desperate and always tied to healing — the 'therapeutic Son of David' pattern. Runs to the entry and the temple (21:9, 15).

son-of-man.note: Daniel 7:13-14 — one like a son of man given everlasting dominion. Runs from 8:20 to the trial and the parousia.

spirit.note: pneuma — conceived of the Holy Spirit (1:18) to the Spirit descending like a dove (3:16) to the Sermon's first beatitude (5:3) to the unforgivable sin against the Spirit (12:31-32).

test.note: peirazō — 'the tester' approaches in the wilderness (4:3); the same verb returns whenever the Pharisees try to trap Jesus.

thorn.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): akantha; few occurrences, all placed. Gen 3:18 echo. Ahead: the crown of thorns (27:29).

throw.note: Unit 8 cluster: the tormented servant thrown down (8:6), the sons of the kingdom cast out (8:12), the fever, the storm. Watch for the dragnet and the outer darkness later.

torment.note: Inclusio inside Unit 8 — the servant tormented by illness (8:6) and the demons fearing torment (8:29). Watch for eschatological torment later.

treasure.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20): unit-06 local root recurring at 12:35.

understand.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): syniēmi. Matthew credits the learners with it where Mark stresses their confusion. Ahead: 15:10; 16:12; 17:13.

urge.note: The centurion entreats (8:5), the demons entreat (8:31), the town entreats him to go (8:34) — the same verb bends from faith to rejection.

wage.note: misthos — 'great is your wage in the skies' (5:12) sets the terms the Sermon keeps returning to: a wage that can be spent early (6:1-16) or never lost (10:42).

weeping-grinding.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): fixed phrase, Matthew's signature refrain. Ahead: 22:13; 24:51; 25:30.

well-pleased.note: eudokēsa — the Father's voice at the baptism (3:17) is the thread's true open; the same word recurs in Jesus' prayer at 11:26.

wise.note: The shrewd builder on rock (7:24); shrewd as snakes for the road (10:16); the faithful and shrewd slave (24:45); the five shrewd virgins (25:2).

withdraw.note: anachōreō — the magi withdraw by another road (2:12); Joseph withdraws to Egypt then Nazareth (2:13-22); Jesus withdraws at news of John's arrest (4:12) and before the ruler's daughter is raised (9:24).

worship.note: proskyneō — the magi's worship (2:2, 2:11) is what the devil demands for himself (4:9) and Jesus refuses him with Deut 6:13; the risen Jesus receives it again at 28:9, 17.

worthy.note: axios — fruit worthy of repentance (3:8) becomes the mission discourse's repeated test of who and what is worthy (10:10-38).
